"''The device has been planted, as you requested.''"
"''Good. You'll be well-rewarded in the new era.|Elia Kane and her informant|}} '''Elia Kane''', designated '''TK-2755''' under the [[Galactic Empire]] and as '''Amnesty Officer G68''' under the [[New Republic]], was a [[human]] who served as an [[Imperial officer]] for the Galactic Empire, a [[Communications officer|comms officer]] in one of its [[Gideon's Imperial remnant|remnants]] led by [[Moff]] [[Gideon]], and later a [[spy]]. During the [[Imperial Era]], Kane trained at the [[Royal Imperial Academy]] on the [[planet]] [[Coruscant]] before the Empire [[Battle of Jakku|fell]] to the New Republic, and eventually joined the remnant forces under the command of Moff Gideon in the [[Outer Rim Territories]]. By [[9 ABY]], Kane was an [[officer]] who liaised with an [[Unidentified Mimbanese worker|informant]] on tracking the [[Force-sensitive]] infant [[Din Grogu|Grogu]] and brought news to Gideon when a tracker had been placed on the [[gunship]] ''[[Razor Crest]]'', the [[starship]] of the [[Mandalorian]] [[Din Djarin]], where the child was being kept. Eventually [[Gideon's light cruiser]] tracked the ''Razor Crest'' to the planet [[Tython]], destroying the gunship. They reported to Gideon that his [[Phase-III Dark Trooper|dark troopers]] were ready, and the Moff had the [[trooper]]s capture Grogu. After, the comms officer joined Gideon in visiting the infant, soon receiving orders to contact [[Doctor]] [[Penn Pershing]]. The comms officer later alerted the moff to a message from Din Djarin, who wished to liberate Grogu from Gideon. When the [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle|''Lambda''-class T-4a shuttle]] [[Operating number|designated]] [[Shuttle 2743]] [[Second rescue of Grogu|arrived]] from [[hyperspace]] near the [[cruiser]], Kane acknowledged the [[shuttle]]'s request to dock but soon ordered the starship to keep clear for deploying [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter|TIE fighters]]. The shuttle failed to comply, and so she ordered the [[TIE series|TIEs]] to keep clear of the launch tube. Djarin and his associates exited the shuttle and engaged the personnel on board. Kane survived the battle and was captured by the New Republic, and integrated into the [[New Republic Amnesty Program]]. However, she remained devoted to the cause of the Empire, and secretly continued to take directions from her superior, Moff Gideon. ==Biography== ===Serving Gideon=== ====Capture of Grogu==== {{Quote|Have the dark troopers been engaged?''"
"''Momentarily.|Gideon and Elia Kane|{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 14: The Tragedy}}}} During the [[Imperial Era|time]] of the [[Galactic Empire]], Elia Kane joined the [[Politics|government]] and trained at the [[Imperial Academy]] on the [[ecumenopolis]] [[Planet|world]] of [[Coruscant]]. The Empire then [[Battle of Jakku|fell]]{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 19: The Convert}} in [[5 ABY]]''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' after losing a [[Galactic Civil War|war]] with the rising [[New Republic]].''[[Aftermath: Empire's End]]'' Kane, though, continued with the Empire's remaining forces, which was made up of remnant factions, and served as a [[communications officer]] in the [[Gideon's Imperial remnant|remnant]] led by [[Moff]] [[Gideon]], holding the [[Military rank|rank]] of [[lieutenant]]. She served on [[Gideon's light cruiser]], where she passed the Imperial [[scientist]] [[Doctor]] [[Penn Pershing]] around a hundred times, though the two never got a chance to introduce themselves to one another. In [[9 ABY]],The events of "[[Chapter 12: The Siege]]" took place in [[9 ABY]] per the reasoning [[Template:MandoDate|here]]. Gideon was [[Hunt for Grogu|hunting]] a [[Force-sensitive]] [[Youngling|infant]] named [[Din Grogu|Grogu]], known to the moff as "the asset." During the hunt, Kane kept in contact with a [[Mimbanese]] [[Unidentified Mimbanese worker|informant]] that operated on the planet [[Nevarro]]. After the [[Mandalorian]] [[bounty hunter]] [[Din Djarin]], Grogu's guardian, [[Second skirmish on Nevarro|visited]] Nevarro with the child, the informant was made to repair on the Mandalorian's [[gunship]], the ''[[Razor Crest]]'', and made contact with Kane, confirming that Grogu was still with Djarin. Kane had the informant to install a [[Homing beacon|tracking beacon]]. When the Mimbanese worker contacted her back to confirm they had done so, she thanked her contact, promising rewards in the "new era." The comms [[Imperial officer|officer]] then made her way to Gideon, informing him of the news she had received from the informant. [[File:GideonsCommOfficer2.png|thumb|left|300px|Elia Kane was stationed on the bridge of Moff Gideon's light cruiser.]] Gideon's [[light cruiser]] tracked the ''Razor Crest'' to the planet [[Tython]], where Gideon's [[stormtrooper]]s [[Battle of Tython (9 ABY)|fought]] Djarin and two of his associates, the [[assassin]] [[Fennec Shand]] and the Mandalorian [[Boba Fett]]. The [[cruiser]] soon destroyed the ''Razor Crest'' while the [[Starship|gunship]] was parked on the ground. When Gideon asked if his [[Phase-III Dark Trooper|dark troopers]] had engaged, the Kane reported that the [[trooper]]s were deploying momentarily, and four dark troopers then flew down to apprehend Grogu at a [[Force-henge|temple ruin]]. Once the infant had been taken aboard the light cruiser, the vessel escaped into [[hyperspace]]. Kane later joined Gideon as he inspected and taunted Grogu. After the moff had the infant [[stun]]ned, he ordered the comms [[officer]] to send an encrypted message to Doctor Pershing once they exited hyperspace to say that they had gotten a donor for him, Kane acknowledging Gideon's order before they both left the cell. ====The Mandalorian strikes back==== {{Quote|Request denied! Please clear launch tube until fighters deploy!''"
"''Negative! Negative! We are under attack!''"
"''Clear launch tube immediately.|Kane and Bo-Katan Kryze, impersonating an Imperial shuttle pilot|{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 16: The Rescue}}}} [[File:MandoThreatensGideon-TMCh15.png|thumb|right|300px|Kane stood witness for Din Djarin's message to Gideon.]] Sometime after, Kane, backed by an [[Unidentified Imperial gunnery officer (Gideon)|Imperial gunnery officer]], alerted Gideon to a holographic message from the Mandalorian. It was simply a recording by Djarin claiming that Gideon underestimated the value of Grogu and that the infant would be back in the Mandalorian's custody shortly. The Kane and gunnery officer stood aside the table displaying the message as Gideon witnessed it for himself.{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 15: The Believer}} A short while later, the Kane was at her terminal when the [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle|''Lambda''-class T-4a shuttle]] [[Operating number|designated]] [[Shuttle 2743]] [[Second rescue of Grogu|arrived]] out of hyperspace near Gideon's cruiser under pursuit from the [[Firespray-31-class patrol and attack craft|''Firespray''-31-class patrol and attack craft]] ''[[Slave I]]''. The comms officer noticed the starships on her scanners and heard as [[Bo-Katan Kryze]] requested emergency docking. The Kane acknowledged the request, believing that Kryze was an Imperial [[pilot]], and Gideon ordered for [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter|TIE fighters]] to be launched. The comms officer advised [[Shuttle]] 2743 to stay clear of the cruiser's launch tube where the [[TIE series|TIEs]] were deployed. As TIE fighters deployed to engage the ''Slave I'', the shuttle failed to change course from the launch tube, and so Kane insisted that the vessel must keep clear until the [[Starfighter|fighters]] have deployed. [[File:CommsOfficerPissed-TMCh16.png|thumb|left|300px|Kane orders Shuttle 2743 to stand down.]] The pilot belayed Kane's order, stressing that the Shuttle 2743 was under attack, and so the comms officer gave orders over comm that the launch tube be cleared immediately. The hangar soon stopped deploying TIEs shortly thereafter to allow the shuttle to land, the ''Slave I'' breaking pursuit and escaping in the meantime. In reality, the shuttle carried Djarin and his allies, who gunned down personnel in the hanger. While Kane consulted her console, Gideon ordered the activation of the dark troopers and departed the bridge. Djarin's associates soon reached the bridge, eliminating the defending [[stormtrooper]]s and officers. ===Integrated into the Amnesty Program=== ====Impromptu reunion==== {{Quote|Have you taken in the sights on Coruscant, Doctor?''"
"''No. I haven't had the time.''"
"''I'd be happy to show you around when you do.''"
"''Thank you.|Kane and Penn Pershing|}} Kane survived the assault from Djarin and his allies, who ultimately seized control of Gideon's cruiser and handed the moff over to the New Republic. The comms officer also fell into the New Republic's custody, which put her through their [[Re-Integration Institute]]. Kane then entered the [[New Republic Amnesty Program]], being given the title "Amnesty Officer G68," and resided in an apartment in [[Amnesty Housing]]. However Kane secretly remained loyal to the Imperial cause and in service of Gideon At some point, she began sneaking out of the residence, and the bounds she was allowed in, visiting a [[Shipyard Depot]] where retired Imperial [[Star Destroyer]]s were kept. One day, Doctor Pershing, who had also fallen into the hands of the New Republic, was transferred from the Re-Integration Institute to be a part of the Amnesty Program. In doing so, he was given a talk at the [[Galaxies Opera House]], where he discussed his work on [[cloning]] to an audience of aristocrats. Kane herself joined the audience in the midst of the talk. Later on, Kane sat at a table in courtyard at Amnesty Housing, having drinks with amnesty officers [[Amnesty Officer G27|G27]], [[Amnesty Officer M34|M34]], and [[Amnesty Officer M40|M40]]. While they socialized, Pershing returned to the residence from the opera house. M34 greeted the doctor and welcomed him to Amnesty Housing, introducing himself as well as Kane and the other two officers. Kane and Pershing recognized one another, the latter remarking that he had not expected to see anyone from Gideon's cruiser. M34 had not known "G68" had worked for Gideon, and G27 and M40 passed on rumors they had heard about what had happened to the moff. Kane claimed that she tried not to think about her former superior anymore, going on to commend the New Republic's rehabilitation program and the opportunity it gave her. As a result, M34 had the group toast to the New Republic. Pershing took a seat with the other amnesty officers, Kane asking the doctor if he had taken in the sights on Coruscant. She offered to show him around when he had the time. G27 asked Pershing what he missed from his days in the Empire, the scientist mentioning the [[Color|yellow]] [[travel biscuit]]s from the Imperial [[ration pack]]s. Kane confirmed M34's remark that those could not be found in the [[Core Worlds]], adding that she preferred the red biscuits. M40 jokingly critiqued her taste for the [[Foodstuff|food]], and the group continued to banter about it. That night, Kane got a box of yellow travel biscuits she had acquired from the [[destroyer]]s in the Shipyard Depot and anonymously delivered them to [[Penn Pershing's apartment|Pershing's apartment]]. ====The set up==== [[File:PershingArrested-TM19.png|thumb|left|300px|Kane betrayed Pershing to the New Republic, leading to his arrest.]] Later on, Kane and Pershing visited Coruscant's [[Monument Plaza]], where a number of [[hologram]]s and pavilions were operating. The pair got [[glowing treat]]s and walked through the plaza. As Pershing was experiencing frustration by the Republic's limitations on his genetic research, Kane led Pershing to a retired Imperial Star Destroyer docked on the surface of Coruscant where he could recover a mobile lab to quietly undertake his research. There, she introduced herself with her full name as Elia Kane. As they departed the ship they were arrested by Republic security, Kane turned on Pershing and delivered him to the Republic for reconditioning using a [[Six-O-Two Mitigator]], a type of [[Mind Flayer]]{{InsiderCite|222|Star Wars: The Mandalorian Season Three Companion|''Star Wars: The Mandalorian'' Season Three Companion}} that they claimed was repurposed to break the Imperial indoctrination. As the procedure began she requested to remain in the observation room, calling Pershing a friend, and when she was left alone she dialed up the strength of the mind flayer significantly, erasing Pershing's memories in the process to keep Gideon's cloning experiments safe from being exposed to the New Republic. ====Internal conflict==== {{Quote|[To Tuttle] I'm requesting authorization and backup for dealing with pirates on Nevarro, sir.''"
"''Perhaps the leaders of Nevarro need to understand why becoming a New Republic signatory is valuable.''"
"''[To G68] By letting them suffer? Sounds like a rather Imperial way of thinking.|Teva and Amnesty Officer G68 butt heads on the Nevarro matter|}} [[File:Teva-Tuttle-Kane-CH21.png|thumb|right|300px|Kane successfully manipulated Colonel Tuttle to refuse sending reinforcements on Nevarro]] When [[Captain]] [[Carson Teva]], received a message from [[High Magistrate]] [[Greef Karga]], about [[Pirate King]] [[Gorian Shard]]'s attack on Nevarro, he went to the New Republic's [[New Republic Coruscant skyscraper (Tuttle's office)|offices]] on Coruscant and made his way to the office of [[Colonel]] [[Tuttle]], Kane came in to ask if the colonel needed anything from the commissary. Tuttle chose to ask Kane about Nevarro, and Teva made note of the pin on her uniform linking her to{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 21: The Pirate}} the [[New Republic Amnesty Program|Amnesty Program]], which comprised of former Imperials that had been captured and put through a reintegration program. Kane brought up Nevarro's position as an independent planet. Despite Teva arguing that they could not leave the planet defenseless, Tuttle brought it up that the backlog of requests from New Republic member-worlds had priority, questioning whether intervening with pirates on an independent planet was worth the resources they had. The captain, though, brought up the reports of Imperial activity related to [[Moff]] Gideon—a [[warlord]]''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian Handbook]]'' who had been captured by Din Djarin and his allies not long before and handed over to the New Republic—and argued that they could be linked to the pirate invasion. Tuttle called Teva's claim a "leap," but the pilot answered with how Gideon had never made it to his trial at the [[New Republic Tribunal]]. With Tuttle trying to bounce over his claims, Teva requested authorization and backup to deal with the pirates on Nevarro. Kane then stepped in, suggesting that Nevarro's leaders needed to understand why joining the New Republic was valuable. Teva called it suffering and said it was an Imperial way of thinking, but the amnesty officer argued that Nevarro needed a "new perspective" to see the light. The captain told Kane that her sort did not see the light, citing that she had been captured, though the ex-Imperial called it liberation. After Tuttle concluded that they would see if they could allocate any additional assets to Teva's matter, the captain warned him that something dangerous was happening and that they needed to act before looking over to Kane and leaving the office, and asked the help of Din Djarin and his [[The Tribe|Mandalorian tribe]]. ====Informing Gideon of Nevarro==== {{Quote|Continue with your mission. I shall deal with our Mandalorian friends.|Moff Gideon to Kane|{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 23: The Spies}}}} [[File:Kane_speaks_with_gideon.png|thumb|left|250x250px|Kane contacted Gideon to inform him of new developments in Nevarro]] Some time after Nevarro's liberation, Kane visited a back alley in a busy entertainment district in Coruscant. There, she rendezvoused with a [[Viper probe droid]] dispatched by Moff Gideon, which she activated via voice command to relay a message to him. After informing Gideon of the [[pirate siege on Nevarro]] and the [[Mandalorian]]s' successful repelling of the invaders, a tip which frustrated the Moff as a united [[Mandalorian resistance]] would be a threat to his [[Mandalore Imperial base|base]] on [[Mandalore]], Kane quickly left the scene. ==Personality and traits== {{Quote|Does he still have the asset?''"
"''Yes. Our source confirmed it.|Gideon and Kane|}} [[File:CommsOfficerInformant-TMCh12.png|thumb|250x250px|Kane confidently negotiated with informants.]] A [[human]], Elia Kane had an athletic build, [[Color|light]] skin, black [[hair]], and brown [[eye]]s. She frequently spoke with Gideon and her associates with a neutral expression and voice. When speaking with a Mimbanese informant, the comms officer kept her voice hushed and urgent, promising the informant rewards in the "new era." When Shuttle 2743 failed to stay clear of the cruiser's launch tube, Kane insistently ordered for the shuttle to stay clear, shouting as she did so, but gave in when the pilot failed to comply.[[The Mandalorian Season 2 Junior Novel|''The Mandalorian Season 2'' Junior Novel]] ==Equipment== Kane [[Clothing|wore]] the standard [[Imperial officer's uniform|uniform]] of an Imperial naval officer, including an [[Imperial kepi]] and two [[code cylinder]]s attached below each shoulder. She wore a [[rank insignia plaque]] on her left [[breast]] with two red bars above two blue, which signified the rank of lieutenant.''[[Star Wars Rebels: Spark of Rebellion]]'' The officer was also armed with a [[SE-14r light repeating blaster]] which she wore on her right hip. After she joined the [[New Republic Amnesty Program]], she began wearing an [[Amnesty uniform]]. ==Behind the scenes== ===Milestones and conception=== {{Quote|A lot of these designs are just little subtle tweaks on what we already know. Here we gave her a new hat, with a couple little points, placing it somewhere between the First Order hats and the Imperial hats of the original trilogy, while injecting a bit of Soviet-era Russian design in there, as well.|Brian Matyas, on his designs of Kane|[[The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian (Season Two)|''The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian'' Season Two]]}} [[File:CommOfficerDesigns.png|thumb|250px|Concept art for the "Comms Officer" by Brian Matyas|left]] Elia Kane first appeared in "[[Chapter 12: The Siege]]," the fourth episode of the [[The Mandalorian Season Two|second season]] of [[Jon Favreau]]'s [[2019]] [[Disney+]] television series ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]'', directed by [[Carl Weathers]] and released on [[November 20]], [[2020]].{{D23|url=everything-new-you-can-stream-on-disney-in-november-2020|text=Everything New You Can Stream on Disney+ in November 2020}} Credited as "Comms Officer," she was played by [[Katy O'Brian]]. Her full name and title of Amnesty Officer G68 were revealed when O'Brian reprised the role in "[[Chapter 19: The Convert]]," the third episode of ''The Mandalorian''{{'s}} [[The Mandalorian Season Three|third season]] which was directed by [[Lee Isaac Chung]] and released on [[March 15]], [[2023]].{{D23|url=everything-new-you-can-stream-on-disney-in-march-2023|text=Everything New You Can Stream on Disney+ in March 2023}} In concept art for the officer, artist [[Brian Matyas]] made most his designs of the character with the Imperial officer's uniform having subtle tweaks. In one, he played around with a red palette Imperial officer's uniform for the character, not knowing whether it was a new concept. In another, the artist gave her a hat that mixed the design of those worn by officers of the Galactic Empire and the [[First Order]] as well as hats from [[Wikipedia:Soviet Union|Soviet]]-era [[Wikipedia:Russia|Russia]]. ===Casting and production=== {{Quote|I also want to add that every time I walk into a scene, I do it to the tempo of The Imperial March. It's on loop in my brain in every scene.|Katy O'Brian|{{Twitter|thekatyo|status/1337823574199918592|[[Katy O'Brian]]|quote=I also want to add that every time I walk into a scene, I do it to the tempo of The Imperial March. It's on loop in my brain in every scene. Try me.|archivedate=20201212181949}}}} According to O'Brian, she auditioned with no knowledge of what the role was for, with fake scripts being used for the audition itself, as the production was extremely secretive. She was cast for her role, without being called back for another audition, around a year prior to the release of "Chapter 12: The Siege" and her scenes were filmed in the [[Wikipedia:United States|US]] state of [[Wikipedia:Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]] between [[December]] [[2019]] and [[February]] 2020, her final shoot being among the last scenes filmed. O'Brian claimed that she received her lines the night before as a secrecy precaution, and her Imperial uniform was one of the original costumes used during the filming of the ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[original trilogy]].{{Spotify|url=episode/1ukBZO3Nd3sYBUz46aOeSb?si=f36FVetiQ_mufyQBmriwtA|text=LITTLE LIGHTSABER DAGGERS (with THE MANDALORIAN'S KATY O'BRIAN)|quote=We interrupt your regularly scheduled voyage to bring you BEN and IAN's conversation with actress and martial artist KATY O'BRIAN from BLACK LIGHTNING, Z NATION and most recently: season 2 of THE MANDALORIAN!}} O'Brian added that while the name of Grogu, which had not yet been public, was in her script, she would choose to refer to "Baby Yoda" with different names in her mind like "Crouton" as Grogu would not stick for her. She found the Mandalorian set to be easier to work within, as it was a closed set with no external noise. Producer [[Dave Filoni]] gave the actor context to their role as a [[lieutenant]] and the props she was given. O'Brian fantasised her prop code cylinders as two lightsaber daggers.{{Spotify|url=episode/5VhtbA8SFVYFpy6ZsHkI4k|text=Katy, Why Did You Push That Button! We're Talking With Comms Officer Katy O'Brian of The Mandalorian!|quote=Today is someday and someday we're talking with Comms Officer, Katy O'Brian from The Mandalorian! We talk perfect dates, lesbian relationship timelines, LGBTQ+ people in our galaxy far, far away! Finally, we're hoping she goes and kicks Moffen-Top Gideon's butt to bring us back that Dark Saber!}} [[File:Gideon-CommsOfficer-GalleryS2.png|thumb|300px|Katy O'Brian and Giancarlo Esposito on set as "Comms Officer" and Moff Gideon.]] The crew also gave O'Brian a thick [[Wikipedia:Nintendo Game Boy|gameboy]]-looking prop, which was a communicator prop from the original trilogy, to be the device she used to communicate with the Mimbanese informant. However, the console was used instead as director Weathers thought the prop was too big to use. In filming that scene, the actor spoke with a cardboard cutout of Din Djarin, with the light of the hologram being generated by a lightbox which O'Brian found very bright when the cutout was removed. She also worked closely with Moff Gideon's actor [[Giancarlo Esposito]], even meeting his children when they visited one day. O'Brian also begged her way into meeting the puppet and robotic models for Grogu. Upon the release of "Chapter 12: The Siege," O'Brian received widespread support from her fans and the [[Wikipedia:LGBT|LGBT]] community, which she is a member of. According to O'Brian on [[Wikipedia:Twitter|Twitter]], during filming of ''The Mandalorian'' she walked onto her scenes resounding "[[The Imperial March]]" in her head, which she matched the tempo of. After her return in ''The Mandalorian'' Season 3, O'Brian claimed that she had been surprised about her return, as she thought her character was dead after the Season 2 finale.{{Twitter|LogoTV|status/1636827551476662277|[[Wikipedia:Logo TV|Logo TV]]|date=2023-03-17|quote=We caught up with @thekatyo to talk all things #TheMandalorian, her upcoming film with Kristen Stewart, and more!|archivedate=20230318192423}} ==Appearances== *[[The Mandalorian Season 2 Junior Novel|''The Mandalorian Season 2'' Junior Novel]] {{Ab|The Mandalorian Season 2 Junior Novel (audiobook)}} *[[The Mandalorian – The Graphic Novel of Season 2|''The Mandalorian'' – The Graphic Novel of Season 2]] *{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 12: The Siege}} {{1st}} *{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 14: The Tragedy}} *{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 15: The Believer}} *{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 16: The Rescue}} *''[[The Mandalorian: The Rescue]]'' *{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 19: The Convert}} {{1stID|Elia Kane and Amnesty Officer G68}} *{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 21: The Pirate}} *{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 23: The Spies}} {{1stID|TK-2755}} ==Sources== *{{DisneyGallery|Disney Gallery: The Mandalorian: Making of Season Two|Making of Season Two}} *''[[Star Wars: Battles that Changed the Galaxy]]'' {{Po}} *[[The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian (Season Two)|''The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian'' Season Two]] *{{SW|url=news/star-wars-celebration-anaheim-2022-guest-announce-4|text=Sam Witwer, Matt Lanter, and Katy O'Brian Set Course for ''Star Wars'' Celebration Anaheim 2022}} *{{SWYouTube|odnRRZKhNPk|The Mandalorian | Season 3 Teaser Trailer | Disney+|sw_url=video/the-mandalorian-season-3-teaser-trailer-disney}} *{{SW|url=news/the-mandalorian-chapter-19-the-convert-highlights|text=Bounty Hunting Highlights: 5 of Our Favorite Moments from ''The Mandalorian'' -
